title: Make context-gauge advisories reflect real pressure over the tool-definition baseline
body:
Outcome: context-gauge advisories mean real pressure. Today a KRN lead session starts near 140k of the gauge's 200k from tool definitions alone (MCP connectors: ahrefs, Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Cloudflare, rss_news, Claude Docs), so the 120k/160k advisories fire on turn one and trigger premature handoffs.
Facts: scripts/claude/context-gauge.ts:94-126 hard-codes 120000/160000 of 200k; jsonl-receiver retro and session-continuity session (2026-10-30) observed ~142k after one tool call.
Decision needed (operator): trim connectors unused by KRN for this project, or calibrate thresholds to the model's real window and measured baseline. Recommendation: trim connectors first (frees real context), then re-measure.
Proof: gauge test with a transcript whose first turn is at the measured baseline yields no advisory; documented baseline measurement.
